title: The Pigeon Poop That Heard the Big Bang
subtitle: How Bell Labs Accidentally Tuned Into the Birth of the Universe
style_profile: Tactile Retro-Digital Ephemera + Swiss Technical Infographic
core_thesis: In 1964, two radio astronomers trying to calibrate a satellite antenna at Bell Labs thought an omnipresent 3.5 Kelvin microwave hiss was caused by pigeon droppings inside their horn antenna. In scrubbing away the droppings, they proved that the static was actually the 13.8-billion-year-old cosmic microwave background—the thermal echo of the Big Bang.
counter_intuitive_hook: The most important cosmological discovery of the 20th century was nearly written off as pigeon poop.

visual_style.canvas: Cream deckle cardstock (#F4EFE6) layered over 1960s Bell Labs technical schematics and deep matte carbon void (#0C0C0C)
visual_style.typography: 1-bit coarse dithered serif with active typewriter cursor (_) and Swiss high-contrast data charts
visual_style.portals: 1960s cathode oscilloscopes, analog radio dials, and pen strip-chart recorders as framing windows
visual_style.motion_cadence: Hybrid: 12-15fps stepped stop-motion on archival cutouts, 30fps smooth waves & CMB visualizers
visual_style.asset_sourcing: Real archival assets first (Wikimedia Commons, NASA, Bell Labs public domain); AI only as fallback

chapters.title: The Annoying Hum at Crawford Hill
key_events: May 1964: Arno Penzias and Robert Wilson take over the 50-foot Holmdel Horn Antenna in Crawford Hill, New Jersey
Antenna originally built for NASA Project Echo and Telstar satellite communications
Goal: Measure radio noise in the Milky Way halo at 4,080 MHz (7.35 cm)
The Anomaly: An unexpected 3.5 Kelvin excess temperature omnidirectionally in the sky

chapters.title: The Elimination of All Reason
key_events: Suspect 1: New York City urban broadcast noise (Pointing away showed zero change)
Suspect 2: Coastal military radar installations (Frequencies did not match)
Suspect 3: 1962 Starfish Prime high-altitude thermonuclear radiation fallout (Decay math failed)
Suspect 4: Terrestrial radio sources or the Milky Way galaxy (Isotropic in all directions, day and night)

chapters.title: The 'White Dielectric Substance'
key_events: Penzias and Wilson climb into the throat/stinger of the horn with flashlights
Two pigeons nesting in the throat coated with droppings ('white dielectric material')
The capture: Trapping the pigeons and mailing them 30 miles away in a box
The return: Pigeons homing back into the antenna
The deep scrub: Scraping droppings, taping seams with aluminum foil
The result: The 3.5 Kelvin hiss remained identical down to 0.1 Kelvin

chapters.title: The 30-Mile Secret at Princeton
key_events: 30 miles away at Princeton University: Robert Dicke, Jim Peebles, and David Wilkinson
Dicke hypothesizes that a hot Big Bang must leave a lingering low-temperature bath (~3K to 5K)
Princeton team begins constructing a small radiometer on the roof of Palmer Physical Laboratory
The phone call: Penzias calls Dicke asking for advice on the unexplained 3.5K excess noise
Dicke hangs up the receiver and tells his team: 'Well boys, we’ve been scooped.'

chapters.title: The Dual Papers & The Death of Steady State
key_events: July 1965: The Astrophysical Journal publishes companion papers
Paper 1: Penzias & Wilson 'A Measurement of Excess Antenna Temperature at 4080 Mc/s' (2 pages, completely understated)
Paper 2: Dicke, Peebles, Roll & Wilkinson 'Cosmic Black-Body Radiation' (The cosmological explanation)
Fred Hoyle's Steady State model effectively disproven overnight
1978 Nobel Prize in Physics awarded to Penzias and Wilson

chapters.title: Tuning Into the Void
key_events: The physics: Photons decoupled 380,000 years after the Big Bang (Recombination Era) stretched into microwaves
Space telescopes: COBE (1992, Smoot & Mather), WMAP (2003), and ESA Planck (2013) all-sky maps
The analog television easter egg: 1% of static snow on untuned analog TVs is the Big Bang afterglow
Closing philosophical reflection: Human curiosity transforming bird droppings into the birth certificate of the universe
